implementation: Bounded OffsetCommit/OffsetFetch8-10 models and caller-driven OffsetClient; ConsumerGroup/Admin UUID routing, assignment-bound synchronous/queued commits, captured metadata projection for named/batched Admin calls, actual-socket negotiation and one offset operation deadline.

bounds.default_limits: wire1MiB; each string64KiB/aggregate1MiB; array8192/aggregate32768; tags64/aggregate1024; payload64KiB; requested decoded4MiB

owned_shutdown: Every final owned peer joins three listeners/workers, rebinds its ports and records zero tasks. The runner parent-waits every final process; Java closes its Admin/manual Consumer and records zero Kafka threads. Typed cancellation observes physical EOF while OffsetClient lives and then reuses it.
retained_failures: All prototype compile/focused/SDK failures and their source captures remain in validation, including4.1 builder signature, private test constructor, old nullable-metadata projection, actual capability wrapper and source-binding selection fixes.

Strict checks rejected blocking test filesystem calls, unused lint expectations, redundant match guards, expect calls, a standard mutex and a manual range pattern. Corrected source and each actual failed command remain; no suppression was added.
Post-review legacy Admin timeout/string admission fix was compiled and tested before final source binding. Earlier accepted SDK/full-suite prototypes remain distinct from final evidence.
An invalid backlog CLI mode is retained separately; only the actual backlog mode supplies the accepted report.
limits: Selected Apache SDK schemas/factories and genuine Java public Admin/manual Consumer calls against bounded scripted peers. No live coordinator persistence, native broker recreation, membership churn or failover qualification.

Java name-based public factories still cap OffsetCommit/OffsetFetch at9 and refuse10-only peers. Genuine generated UUID builders and full data schemas accept10. These are different public surfaces; no v10 Java manual Consumer operation is invented.

Typed offset requests preserve raw UUIDs, nullable metadata and terminal errors. Legacy named projections retain their existing empty-string metadata projection and fail on unmapped UUIDs; all-topic raw results preserve unknown UUIDs.

UUID mutations retry the same request at most eight times; lost replies, timeout and cancellation remain ambiguous. The tests simulate same-name recreation by changing Metadata/assignment UUIDs, including rebalance and queued commits.

New typed operations own at most two additional sockets and no background task. Existing Admin/group/consumer connections, caches, heartbeat workers and asynchronous-commit queue policies are unchanged; this is not a global resource ceiling.

Requested storage limits do not measure allocator overhead or RSS. Shared bounded ApiVersions/TLS/SASL/frame transport is unchanged. New decoding validates body/count/string/tag/storage budgets before its own collection allocations.

Names use legacy8/9 in the typed client; UUID intent never falls back. Existing name-based methods retain earlier-version layouts and re-negotiate actual coordinator ranges. Named Admin calls use fresh bounded Metadata10-13; group commits use captured assignment IDs.

The new UUID path and existing Admin offset methods use an original operation deadline. Existing group membership/rejoin and general metadata refresh APIs have their own lifecycle limits; no overall group startup deadline is newly qualified.

Warm connection reuse and throughput are not measured here. No fastest-client/server, production, core/full conformance, hosted CI, main merge or release claim. Required conformance denominator and independent-case count stay182/51.
